slowdown.note: He signed the 23 September 2026 letter, which asks for a formal agreement with China "that would slow down" frontier AI development to prevent cyberattacks, biological weapons and other dangers. This is a signed letter, not a statement of his own.

pause.note: The letter he signed asks for an agreement with China that would "potentially enact a mutual pause" in frontier AI development; this is a possible pause, conditional on China joining, not a call for an outright halt. Separately, his 3 June 2025 floor speech opposed an "AI moratorium", but that was the proposed 10-year ban on state AI regulation, not a pause in AI development, so it does not bear on this position.
sources: Van Hollen press release with full letter

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI. The letter he signed mentions that automation of AI research may speed up progress, but does not call for a ban.

record: Signed the letter from 17 Senate Democrats, led by Sen. Van Hollen, urging President Trump to negotiate a formal agreement with China on frontier AI, including a slowdown and possible mutual pause.
Joined a statement by ten Senate Foreign Relations Committee Democrats on the Trump-Xi summit that welcomed US-China AI talks while calling for strict AI chip export controls.

Reintroduced, with Sen. Padilla, the Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations (FAIR) Elections Act, banning false AI-generated election content meant to suppress voters (outside this project's scope: elections, not catastrophic risk).

Gave a Senate floor speech opposing the proposed 10-year ban on state and local AI regulation, saying he would raise a point of order against it, and promoting his AI Civil Rights Act (outside this project's scope: bias and civil rights, not catastrophic risk).

Signed, with Sens. Markey and Welch, a letter to Google's chief executive questioning the removal of the company's pledge not to build AI for weapons or surveillance (military and surveillance use, outside this project's scope).

Signed a letter led by Sen. Wyden urging the Trump administration to restore export controls on advanced technology, including AI chips, to China (competition with China, outside this project's scope).
grade_reason: The only evidence at level A is the 23 September 2026 letter he co-signed, which calls advanced AI a technology that poses an existential threat and says its misuse could threaten humanity. Six web searches found no statement in his own individual words about catastrophic AI risk; his own remarks on AI concern bias, privacy, elections and surveillance.
notes: All six required web searches ran this time (11 November 2026); no extra searches were run. They turned up no statement by Merkley in his own words on superintelligence, extinction, loss of control, AI and bioweapons, or a pause or slowdown, so the grade still rests entirely on the co-signed 23 September 2026 letter; a reviewer may prefer to weigh that lower than a personal statement. New material from the searches is all level D or record-only: his 3 June 2025 floor speech (Congressional Record), the 19 February 2025 letter to Google, and the 13 November 2025 export controls letter. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: no source found shows Merkley as a co-sponsor. The Fortune/Associated Press report of 23 September 2026 (https://fortune.com/2026/09/23/bernie-sanders-superintelligent-ai-ban) names only Sen. Sanders and Rep. Casar; no co-sponsor list was seen, so this is unknown rather than a confirmed 'no'. Caution for reviewers: search summaries described Merkley as opposing an 'AI moratorium'; that refers to the 10-year ban on state AI regulation, not a pause in AI development, and is not counted as a position. Quotes were checked by a script as exact continuous passages of the downloaded page text (the four letter quotes against the Van Hollen page, the joint statement against Merkley's page, the floor speech against the congress.gov Congressional Record page), all re-downloaded today. Pages opened but not used: Congressional Digest November 2025 (a paywalled reprint of the same floor speech); Al Jazeera 26 March 2026 on the data center moratorium bill and the Fortune article (neither mentions Merkley); Merkley's 11 March 2026 release on a letter to the Defense Department about strikes in Iran (the search summary says it raised AI target selection; military use, level D, not quoted). One search result, letsdatascience.com on the Sanders-Casar bill, could not be opened (error 403). Not opened because they concern privacy or other out-of-scope topics: Ban Flock Act (2 October 2026), facial recognition moratorium bill (25 September 2026), ICE Out of Our Faces Act (February 2026), biometric smart glasses letter (14 May 2026), Algorithmic Accountability Act co-sponsorship.
